summary: Iter16 — Stripe Subscription Billing + commission accrual + per-chapter audiobook export fully verified. All 34 new tests in /app/backend/tests/test_billing.py pass (incl. real Stripe test-mode checkout session creation against the live preview backend with STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_test_emergent). The 14 iter15 regression tests still pass; supervisor shows backend RUNNING.

minor.issue: Endpoint hits Stripe API (~1-2s) on every poll. Consider short-circuiting when payment_transactions.processed=true AND txn is older than N seconds, to avoid repeat Stripe calls during long /dashboard polls.

The underlying emergentintegrations wrapper surfaces 'Unexpected error processing webhook: \'type\'' for empty-body posts. Acceptable (returns 400) but the message leaks an internal KeyError-style detail. Consider catching and returning a friendly 'invalid webhook payload' string.
PUT-only; there is no GET. iter15 tests work around it by reading via the public /affiliate/settings. Not a bug — just worth noting that admin UI uses public GET + admin PUT.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~2200 lines. Strongly recommend extracting billing routes (lines ~600–970) into /app/backend/routers/billing.py and chapter-audiobook routes into /app/backend/routers/audiobook.py before adding more features. The mandate is <700 lines per file; this file is 3x over.

_credit_successful_payment correctly marks the transaction processed BEFORE inserting the commission row, which is the right order for idempotency, but the commission insert is best-effort with a broad `except Exception` — if Mongo is briefly unavailable the commission is permanently lost. Consider a small retry queue (e.g. write a commissions_dlq doc) so payouts are recoverable.

Webhook handler calls client.get_checkout_status again after handle_webhook to fetch amount_total — that is 2 Stripe round-trips per webhook. The Stripe wrapper already returns the session payload in event; reuse it if possible to halve latency.

billing_checkout sets metadata['user_id'] from the authenticated user but the helper later trusts metadata['user_id'] from Stripe. If someone could ever craft a session via a third-party tool, this could matter — defense-in-depth: prefer txn.user_id over metadata.user_id for the credit operation.

chapter_audiobook.export_chapters_zip is fully sequential — for a 30-chapter book at OpenAI TTS speed (~30s/chapter), that's 15 minutes of one HTTP request held open. Consider streaming or backgrounding it (queue + poll) when the user count grows. Not blocking for MVP.
POST /documents/{id}/audiobook/chapters takes voice & speed as query params, not body — inconsistent with the single-shot /audiobook endpoint. Worth aligning before the frontend wires both.
No rate limit on /billing/checkout — a malicious user could spam Stripe Checkout creates. The Stripe test key has its own rate limit, but a 5/min user-level limiter would be cheap insurance.

iter14's /app/backend/tests/test_affiliate.py still contains 3 stale tests (flagged in iter15 already) — they pre-date the schema rename and continue to fail. Not iter16's responsibility, just flagging again.
test_credentials: Owner bagmoneyceo@gmail.com / Surfwall1 verified; regular users registered on the fly with TEST_iter16_* prefix.
seed_data_creation: Each module run registers ~3-4 fresh TEST_iter16_* users and creates ~5 small TEST_iter16_doc documents. Real Stripe test-mode session(s) created via /billing/checkout (no payment completed — session creation alone proves the integration). One payment_transactions row is inserted per test run; rows are status='initiated' and harmless to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Per-chapter audiobook real-MP3 generation was NOT exercised end-to-end (skipped per the review_request to keep test runtime <30s). Only validation paths (0-chapter / 1-chapter / wrong-owner) were tested. If a future iteration touches narrate_audiobook or the OpenAI TTS pipeline, manually trigger /documents/{id}/audiobook/chapters with a 2-chapter doc and ~200 chars each — expect a ~5-8s response and a ZIP containing 2 MP3s + 1 tracklist.txt. Also: Stripe webhook signature verification was NOT mocked end-to-end (signature validation is inside emergentintegrations and we can't easily forge a valid signature); only the rejection-of-bad-payload path is asserted. If a real Stripe webhook ever fires in this preview env, look in backend logs for 'Stripe webhook handling failed' to confirm signature wiring.
